subject: C19
required_fixes: R4 — Validate completion item identifiers before creating transcript entries. crates/desktop-core/src/harness/session.rs:859-869 accepts an arbitrary string item.id, and the new complete fallback at lines 958-965 inserts it into HarnessEntry.id without the bounded_id check used by item/started. A matching-thread/turn item/completed notification with a 301-character item ID and text 'OK' is only 436 bytes, passes the frame limits, and creates a 305-character native entry ID ('u-1/' plus the item ID). packages/desktop-contracts/src/client.ts:952-964 rejects entry IDs longer than 300, so the full shell snapshot becomes unconsumable. The independent production-parser probe confirmed rejection of this projected entry and acceptance with a valid item ID. Acceptance: apply the existing bounded identifier policy before completion can create or update an entry, reporting a sanitized protocol failure for invalid IDs without publishing an invalid snapshot. Add a production-interface stand-in case for an overlong completion ID with no matching started item, and verify that legitimate completion-without-deltas behavior and the full snapshot contract still pass.
limitations: All four supplied fingerprints recompute exactly. Verified 638 source-inventory entries, 342 packet references, run logs/artifacts, before/after inputs and exact command sequences. C18 and P05 predecessor receipts have passing verdicts with matching request/verdict/raw-output bindings. Compared all seven changed source files against the hash-verified attempt-04 source reconstructed from its packet.

Attempt-04 R1-R3 are closed. Completed text now observes per-turn and transcript limits, accounts for replacement text and truncates on UTF-8 boundaries. Tests cover oversized final text, multiple answer items and transcript exhaustion. Failed-answer status now discloses up to five possible attempts and possible processing. Unsafe u64 token counters are omitted, and the safe-integer contract remains intact. R4 is a new invalid-identifier path introduced by creating entries for previously unstarted completions.

Inspected implementer-run logs report 389 desktop tests, 187 Core library tests, 13 Harness process integration tests and five OS supervision tests. All 40 mutation probes report named guard failures against seven matching source-input hashes; five baseline targets passed three times each. The new probes challenge completion bounds, cumulative answer accounting, unsafe counters and the retry statement, but not R4. Application builds and on-disk application suites were not independently rerun.

All ten current C19 native checks pass against fixture executable 35d6c093bac0d18769b467a069c9263354f57fc9b390bcee7cdcdb744469fab9. The 212 C01-C18 native regression checks remain bound to attempt-04 executable 646cf8dc2f2d776c4efb644c3ea442b930d5ea204747c216330e3d1819eccb2c, as the packet discloses; they are historical regression evidence, not current-bundle runs. Production changes are confined to Harness completion/counter handling and status text. The C17 change only strengthens a test's wait for its first saved file. The engine, archive, pin, launcher and authority admission/retirement implementation are unchanged from attempt-04. This review remains within C19's fixture-backed runtime/lifecycle scope. Live service qualification is C25, sign-in/refresh and protected history C20, tools/project access C21 and MCP C22.
